title: Behavior: hunt loops, grinding, tours, patrols and looting
tagline: The top-level loops that decide, look by look, where she hunts, what she shoots and which drops she takes.
summary: The top of the stack: the loops that run for minutes or hours and decide what to do next. `Hunt` (the hunt loop) and its subclass `Grind` (the default) make one decision after every look by an ordered list of rules; `Patrol` and `Tour` hold the map knowledge they choose from; the loot sweep, the loot chain and the `Looter` decide which drops to pick up and how. `bootstrap` reads her max HP, level and DEF from perception, and `walk` is a movement-only test drive.
details_md:
### Words used here

A **look** is one perception snapshot (a `Scene`): most search the **band** around her (140 units above to 75 below her feet, gamelab/docs/hunt-modes.md), some the **whole screen**. A **ground** is a platform worth hunting; a **spot** is where she stands to shoot it (often a platform above it, out of its monsters' reach). A **pile** is a kill's drops (or drops seen on the ground), kept by the drop store; the **ledger** places each EXP gain on the monster that died (both in behavior/ledger.py, another slice). The **navigator** (control layer) plans and plays chains of jumps, drops, climbs and walks to a platform and x; a **trip** is one such errand.

### Three generations of the same job

| Mode | Command | Module | How it decides |
|---|---|---|---|
| tour | `python -m gamelab tour` | `tour.py` | a fixed sweep of hunting platforms; each stop a fight (`Hunter.clear`) then a loot collection |
| hunt loop (camping) | `tour --loop --camp` | `hunt.py` | one decision per look; stays at a ground until its EXP rate falls below the best other ground's |
| grinding (default) | `tour --loop` | `grind.py` + `patrol.py` | the hunt loop going round a loop of stops over the map's spawn points, leaving a stop as soon as staying pays less than going on |

All three are started by `cmd_tour` in `gamelab/__main__.py`, inside `on_alarm(hunter)` (a Lie Detector makes her retreat), and end standing by on a safe platform (the loops then `park`).

### A pass of the hunt loop

Every pass: **look** (the band around her, the whole screen when needed) -> **book** new kills from the ledger -> **guards** (stuck guard, potions and the safety stop, objective backstop) -> **rules**, first match wins: close quarters and a valuable pile always first; then, travelling, in passing, finish and the loot sweep; at the ground, high ground, shoot, better spot, then stay (sweep or wait) or leave (sweep on the way out, advance) -> **one step**: a throw, a short walk along her platform, a navigator trip, or a stand on a pile. A respawn or a new pile changes the next step within a second or two.

Trips are the navigator's (control layer), in `TRANSIT` mode, and the navigator asks the loop's `_interrupt` before every chain of moves. Control may not import behavior (tests/test_architecture.py), so the loop steers it through that callback. What she's heading for is an `Objective` on a stack: a higher rule suspends it rather than ending it, and its clock (60 s) keeps running.

### Loot

Kills placed by the ledger become expected piles in the drop store (behavior/ledger.py, another slice). Each look, the loop turns the store's candidates into pick spots (`Hunt._spots`): their worth (looting's prices), stand time, landing time, survival, the monsters that would meet her there (shot first if she can, else the pile waits), and the seconds each may add to her way (3 s fresh, down to 1 s at 60 s old). `sweep.plan` solves the best itinerary exactly; `Sweeper` keeps it unless another is clearly better. EXP comes first: with anything in reach no pile goes ahead. In grinding with the target-first planner and the whole screen (both on by default), the itinerary's next few piles (4 at most) run as one navigator chain (`lootchain`). `Looter` keeps her inventory tabs and serves the old tour's walk-and-mop-up looting.

### Where to hunt

The hunt loop picks grounds from the `Tour`'s value map (lab/grounds.json): EXP a visit blended from spawn data and real visits, divided by travel plus visit length. Grinding uses `Patrol`: spawn points, one stop per platform, a `Belief` of each point's monsters (memory, a learned memoryless refill rate, the census of the whole map held to its cap), the loop of 2-12 stops with the best long-run EXP a minute, and the next stop (the loop's, a pile of seen monsters that pays 1.25x the loop over its detour, or a census trip when her view looks starved).

### Design stance

The fight rules hold measured lessons (high ground, facing, end margins), so they stay rules, not one weighted score; scores are used only where places are compared by time (spots, piles, grounds, stops). Most thresholds are marked "guess" in the code: starting values tuned in the simulator harness's A/B runs, with the README recording each change's measured effect. Every choice is logged in words and sent as telemetry ('hunt', 'grind', 'sweep', 'loot_chain', 'summary') for the mini-map and later analysis.

modules.title: The hunt loop (Hunt)
modules.tagline: One decision after every look: the first rule that applies picks her next step.
modules.summary: `Hunt` is "hunt mode" from gamelab/docs/hunt-modes.md. Instead of a tour's fixed stops, loot trips and fights on the way, it takes a look, books new kills, checks her health, and lets the first rule that applies choose one step: a throw, a short walk, a navigator trip toward an objective, or a stand on a pile of drops. On its own it hunts one ground at a time (`tour --loop --camp`) and leaves by a rate rule; `Grind` subclasses it for the default grinding mode.
modules.details_md:
`Hunt` sits on top of a `Tour` (for the map knowledge: the value map, the kinds worth hunting, the safe platforms and spots) and the tour's `Hunter` and `Navigator`. `run(minutes)` loops `_pass()` until time is up, then walks to a safe platform (`Tour.stand_by` in `TRANSIT` mode) and sums the run into a `HuntReport`.

### One pass (`_pass`)

1. **Look** (`_look`): the band around her plus her platform's drops; the whole screen once a far kill's drops have landed (`FAR_DROPS_LOOK`), and a whole-screen look at most every `WIDE_EVERY` (2 s) when the rules need one (`_wide`).
2. **Book** (`_book`): new kills from the ledger, credited to the current `Visit` only once she has arrived and only for kills on the ground (or made from it or its spot); a pile seen gone after she went for it counts as progress.
3. **Guards**: the stuck guard (`_stuck`, 120 s with no kill, pick-up or new ground), `Hunter.health_check` (potions, and the safety stop, which raises), and the objective backstop (`OBJECTIVE_S`, 60 s, suspensions included).
4. **Rules** (the design's numbers), first match wins: rule 1, then rule 6a; then, travelling (an objective is set): 4, 4b, the sweep, else on with the trip; at the ground: 2, 3, 7, then the rate rule: staying, the sweep's round trip else 9; leaving, the sweep's piles on her way out, then 11.

| # | Rule | In short |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | close quarters | a target on (or just beside) her platform too close for her next attack: the stance's answer, no closing in |
| 6a | valuable pile | a drop worth `valuable` mesos or more within 15 s of travel, only with nothing in reach (EXP before loot) |
| 4 | in passing | throw at what's in reach, or step at most 150 out from under one above; 15 s per platform per objective |
| 4b | finish | monsters she hurt and didn't kill, 8 s per objective |
| S | sweep | the loot sweep's piles on her way, a round trip from her spot, or on her way out |
| 2 | high ground | on a platform she can't safely stand on (or away from the ground): back to the spot |
| 3 | shoot | a target in reach from where she can stand: `attack.stance`'s answer |
| 7 | better spot | another spot reaches 2 more (or 1.5x as many) remembered monsters, within 8 s |
| 9 | wait | stand still, walk to a safer place along her platform, or hang on a rope |
| 11 | advance | a trip to the next ground's spot |

5. **One step.** Trips go through the navigator (`_travel`: `Navigator.begin`/`step`), which asks `_interrupt` before each chain of moves, so a monster coming into reach or a pile appearing cuts the trip and the next pass decides.

### Objectives are suspended, not ended

`self.obj` is the current `Objective` (a spot or a pile); a higher rule pushes it onto `self.stack` and pops it back later, keeping its route weights and its clock. The clock runs while it's suspended, which bounds a "shoot respawns on the way forever" loop.

### Leaving a ground

`_leaving` is the rate rule: her EXP a second here (with a 20 s prior at the ground's expected rate, times `1 - 2 x danger` of the spot) against the best other ground's EXP a second including travel; she leaves under 0.8 of it, after at least 15 s or 6 throws. The fast exit leaves when looks covering 75% of the ground saw nothing wanted for 3 s and no kill of hers is due back (`RESPAWN` 8 s + 2); that ground is then skipped 120 s. With no other ground to go to, she stays and waits. Leaving, `_leave` first sweeps the piles on her way out (within `DEPART_BUDGETS`), then `_next_ground` picks by value / (travel + visit length), varied by a random 0.75-1.25.

Most numbers are marked "guess" in the code: starting values tuned in the simulator's A/B runs (`gamelab.sim.harness`), not measured in game.

key_items.name: Hunt
key_items.signature: class Hunt: def __init__(self, tour, log=print, rng: random.Random | None = None)
key_items.summary: The hunt loop over a Tour's map knowledge, its hunter and its navigator. Holds the visit, the objective stack, the fight state, the loot sweeper and every clock.
key_items.details_md: Many small methods (`_through`, `_chain_over`, `_land_near`, `_instead_of_waiting`, `_varies`, `_ends_on_arrival`, `_whole`, `_guards_it`, `_none_landed`, `_fill`, `_among`, `_may_stop_her`, `_home`) return the hunt loop's plain default and exist so `Grind` can override them.

key_items.name: Hunt.run
key_items.signature: def run(self, minutes: float) -> HuntReport
key_items.summary: Hunt for `minutes`, then stand by on the nearest safe platform; returns the run's report and emits the telemetry 'summary' record.
key_items.details_md: Before the loop it installs hooks: `Looter.yield_to = _yields` (picking up stops for what's in reach), `Looter.unseen` and `Attacks.unseen` (monsters a look missed). The loop catches `LookLost` (stand still until `Senses.regain` brings the game back, shifting every clock with `_paused`), `KeyDoubt` (runs `Hunter.check_keys`), and `ChatDue`/`StatsDue` (collapses the chat box or reads the stat window at a quiet moment). After the stand-by trip `_book_after` books the kills made on the way to stand by.

key_items.name: Hunt._pass
key_items.signature: def _pass(self) -> str | None
key_items.summary: One look and one step: bookkeeping, the stuck guard and health check, the objective backstop, then rule 1, rule 6a, then `_while_travelling` (an objective is set) or `_at_ground`. Returns "stop" to end the hunt.

key_items.name: Hunt._at_ground
key_items.signature: def _at_ground(self, s: Scene, targets, visible, hidden, now: float) -> str | None
key_items.summary: At the ground: high ground (2), back to spot, shoot (3), better spot (7), then the rate rule: stay (sweep a round trip, else wait) or leave.

key_items.name: Hunt._while_travelling
key_items.signature: def _while_travelling(self, s: Scene, targets, visible, hidden, now: float) -> str | None
key_items.summary: With an objective: a valuable-pile trip goes on or is called off; else in passing (4), finish (4b), the sweep's pile trip or piles on her way, else on with the trip.

key_items.name: Hunt._leaving
key_items.signature: def _leaving(self, s: Scene) -> str | None
key_items.summary: The rate rule: why she leaves now (a string for the log) or None to stay.
key_items.details_md: Checks in order: `GROUND_S` (600 s backstop); the fast exit (ground covered by `GROUND_SEEN` 75% of the look, nothing wanted in her memory, nothing due back, confirmed for `EMPTY_CONFIRM_S` 3 s; the ground skipped `SKIP_S` 120 s); patience run out with nothing due back ("nothing came into reach"); then, past `MIN_STAY`/`MIN_THROWS`, `_rate_here() < LEAVE_MARGIN x _best_rate()`. If `_elsewhere()` says no other ground would be picked, `_stay` turns the reason into waiting (live on 2026-10-24 with one ground the reason fired about once a second for 11 minutes).

key_items.name: Hunt._next_ground
key_items.signature: def _next_ground(self, s: Scene) -> None
key_items.summary: Records the finished visit, picks the next ground by value / (travel + visit length) x random 0.75-1.25 x rival share x safe share, and sets a new Visit and a spot objective.
key_items.details_md: With every ground skipped it takes the soonest back. `GROUND_TIE` (off, 0.0) would let grounds within that share of the best take turns.

key_items.name: Hunt._travel
key_items.signature: def _travel(self, rule: str) -> None
key_items.summary: Carries out the objective as one navigator trip: `Navigator.begin(..., until=self._interrupt, mode=TRANSIT)` then `nav.step` until it's over; arrived, stopped 'in position' (next pass decides), or failed (objective dropped).
key_items.details_md: The trip's seconds are `max(5, OBJECTIVE_S - age)`, its route weights and route choice are the objective's (kept across suspensions), and it starts from the latest look if still fresh. A spot never reached gets its ground skipped and a new ground chosen (`_drop_objective`).

key_items.name: Hunt._interrupt
key_items.signature: def _interrupt(self, s: Scene) -> bool
key_items.summary: Asked by the navigator before every chain of a trip: whether a rule now calls for her (close quarters, a pile no longer worth it, a valuable pile that goes first, a wound to finish, a target in reach she may shoot, or the sweep has a different pile for her).
key_items.details_md: This is how behavior steers control without control importing behavior (tests/test_architecture.py's layer rule). Only asks what the next pass would act on: a monster only a jump reaches stopped every trip on its first look in `loop_tree_walls` (107 s held, found 2026-10-25).

key_items.name: Hunt._sweep
key_items.signature: def _sweep(self, s: Scene, dest: tuple[int, float] | None, say: bool = True) -> "sweep.Stop | None"
key_items.summary: The loot sweep's next stop from look `s` on her way to `dest`: builds pick spots (`_spots`), the terms (`_sweep_terms`: lull budget or way-out budget), and calls `sweep.Sweeper.solve`; logs and emits a 'sweep' record when the itinerary changes.
key_items.details_md: Solved once per look per destination (keyed on the Scene object itself, not its id).

key_items.name: Hunt._spots
key_items.signature: def _spots(self, s: Scene) -> tuple[list["sweep.Spot"], dict]
key_items.summary: Turns the drop store's candidate piles into `sweep.Spot`s: middle of the drops, worth she can take, stand time, landing time, survival curve, guards, and the seconds each may add to her way (`_allow`).
key_items.details_md: `_allow` gives `ALLOW_FRESH` (3 s) to piles up to `FRESH_S` old (the ledger's 15 s ownership), falling linearly to `ALLOW_OLD` (1 s) at `OLD_S` (60 s), scaled by the share she can take; a pile `SAFER_MARGIN` (0.05) more dangerous than where she stands gets at most `ALLOW_OLD`. Piles left out are explained in the itinerary's `out` ("unsafe: a horny-mushroom at x 890 on 23 would meet her there").

key_items.name: Hunt._guards
key_items.signature: def _guards(self, s: Scene, p: Pile, at: float, stand: float) -> tuple[tuple, str | None]
key_items.summary: "No touch for loot": which monsters would meet her standing on the pile from `at` s for `stand` s plus `sweep.STAND_PAST_S`; those a star from here hits are guards to shoot first, any other leaves the pile out for this look.
key_items.details_md: Monsters come from `_about`: the look's and the feed's swept ones, plus those the look missed (`_unseen`), of kinds that count as a danger, on the pile's platform or (BESIDE_GUARDS) on one just under or over whose bodies would meet hers; never her own kill dying there. Each walks per `_reach_of` (its heading at its kind's speed, turning at its platform's walk edges) through `sweep.meets`.

key_items.name: Hunt._stand
key_items.signature: def _stand(self, s: Scene, pile: Pile) -> None
key_items.summary: Picks up a pile from beside it: each bunch of seen drops walked to from the nearer end and pressed (one press per drop plus one), or for an unseen kill pile a walk over `SPREAD` (30) units either side.
key_items.details_md: Only if nothing would meet her there now. A drop still where she stood twice goes to `Looter.cant_pick`; a pile of only full-tab items costs a try and no walk. Counts one of the pile's `PILE_TRIES` (3) and emits a 'pick' event.

key_items.name: Hunt._respawn_guard
key_items.signature: def _respawn_guard(self, s: Scene, pile: Pile, t0: float) -> str | None
key_items.summary: The spawn guard: holds a short trip to a pile whose stand would meet the map's next respawn pass near free spawn points of monsters that hurt, when the expected touches cost more than waiting.
key_items.details_md: Asked by `_go_for` only for a pile TRIP_AHEAD_S (3 s) away or less, and only once the hunter's spawn clock (`localization.spawnclock`) is sure. Each free point within `RESPAWN_NEAR` (70) is priced at fill x (`NEWBORN_TOUCH` 0.85 - `NEWBORN_SEEN` 0.29) x the share of touches that hurt x the touch's HP in potions; she waits ("<rule>: the pass") if going costs more than the wait at her EXP a second, stepping off a point first if she's on one (`_off_points`).

key_items.name: Hunt._wait
key_items.signature: def _wait(self, s: Scene, targets) -> None
key_items.summary: Rule 9: wait where she is (0.1 s), or step up to `WAIT_STEP` (100) units to a safer place along her platform that keeps the ground's spawn points in reach (`_wait_place`), or hang on a rope (`_refuge`).
key_items.details_md: A safer place must be `WAIT_GAIN` (0.03 of her HP by `attack.danger`) safer; a rope `ROPE_GAIN` (0.05 of the HP she has left) safer, and she gets off it to shoot, when nothing is due back and another ground waits, or after `HANG_MAX_S` (60 s). Never on a map where nothing counts as a danger.

inputs: every look (Scene) from the hunter's Senses: her place, monsters, drops, players, HP
the ledger's kills and the drop store's piles (behavior/ledger.py, through the hunter)
the Tour's value map (ground_values, hunting_grounds, stats) and the navigator's route planner times
attack.danger (the hunter's map danger), attack.spots (spots, spot_for), attack.stance (what to do up close)
the hunter's memory of monsters, spawn clock, attacks (kill times) and Looter (inventory tabs)
outputs: key plans through Actions (throws, walks, pick-up presses) and navigator trips (Navigator.begin/step)
visits recorded into the value map (Tour.record_visit: gamelab/lab/grounds.json)
telemetry records 'hunt' (rule, objective, rates, piles), 'tour', 'sweep', 'monsters', 'event' and one 'summary'
a HuntReport (printed by `tour --loop` as "hunt done: ...")

files_io.what: the value map, through the Tour: each visit's EXP and length (record_visit)
the run's records through gamelab/telemetry.py ('hunt', 'tour', 'sweep', 'summary', events)

modules.concurrency: No threads of its own: it runs on the `tour --loop` command's main thread (or the simulator harness's), blocking on looks and key plans, sleeping 0.1-0.2 s when it waits. Keys reach the game through the separate elevated key player process via the navigator and Actions.

decisions.what: The hunt loop built behind `tour --loop` in the simulator (hunt-modes.md steps 0-5 and 7).
decisions.why: A tour's separate trips each had their own budget and idea of when to fight, and none could say "this has stopped paying, leave"; in the simulator the loop made 114.2 EXP a minute against the fixed tour's 84.8.

decisions.what: EXP before loot: no pile goes ahead of shooting what's in reach (`_loot_first`, `Looter.yield_to`).
decisions.why: The user: "The hunt should be driven by maximizing the exp gain".

decisions.what: No resting: her pet drinks potions and HP staying low ends the hunt (the safety stop).
decisions.why: The user: "Just remove the sit recover hp functionality, it's no longer needed".

decisions.what: The five loot rules (pile here, on the way, urgent, lull loot, loot elsewhere) replaced by one loot sweep, with "no touch for loot" guards.
decisions.why: Live she picked up 199 of 299 mesos a minute seen and lost 100: 47% waiting on PILE_CLEAR, 28% known and never gone for; the user: "try not to hit by mobs just for picking up loots".

decisions.what: Monsters on a platform just under or over a pile count as its guards (BESIDE_GUARDS).
decisions.why: In the simulator a pile on 9 was stood on with Horny Mushrooms walking 8 and 10 by it: four touches.

decisions.what: Piles priced in seconds they may add to her way (`_allow`), not by an exchange of mesos for EXP.
decisions.why: The user: "I'm not sure about this currency conversion. My idea is just picking up mesos and items as we kill mobs".

decisions.what: PET_LOOT turned off.
decisions.why: It put her piles off for her pets, against "piles should be picked up soon after killing" (the user's word); its gain was the simulator's pets'.

decisions.what: HuntReport counts to the end of the stand-by trip, with `casts` for every throw of hers.
decisions.why: R1 of 2026-11-02 reported 52 kills where the run had 53: the stand-by trip's kill and the navigator's shots were missed.

decisions.what: The spawn guard (RESPAWN_GUARD): trips to piles held for the map's respawn pass.
decisions.why: The cornered clip's R3; the user: "good to merge".

gotchas: The rule numbers are the design's, not the order tried: at a ground rule 6a is tried right after rule 1, and the sweep comes after shooting.

An objective's clock keeps running while it's suspended and while rules 1-4 shoot: that bounds a shoot-respawns-on-the-way loop, but it also means a long fight on the way can drop the objective (logged as OBJECTIVE_S).
When looks are lost (LookLost) `_paused` shifts every clock by the pause, so a long pause isn't 'stuck'; the game's own clocks (respawns, drop lives) are not shifted.
A ground no standable spot reaches (the basin) counts as reached anywhere on it: waiting to reach the spot's x, close monsters interrupted her for good.
Kills count for a visit only after she arrived and only on the ground (or from it or its spot); others are 'on the way'.

With only one ground (`--grounds 23`, or a one-ground value map) every reason to leave but the GROUND_S backstop becomes 'stay' and waiting (`_elsewhere`, `_stay`), or she'd make one-second visits forever.
The stuck guard first raises a KeyDoubt 'stall' (behavior.keycheck) to check whether her keys moved in the game's bindings; only if that doesn't fix it does she stand by.
`_sweep_calls` on a made-up look (Scene.what_if, the navigator's look ahead) saves and restores the sweeper's state, so a hypothetical solve can't replace the itinerary she's on.

modules.title: Grinding (Grind)
modules.tagline: The hunt loop going round the map like a player grinds, never camping one ground.
modules.summary: `Grind` subclasses `Hunt` and is the default with `tour --loop` (since 2026-10-27). Instead of the value map's grounds, its stops come from `Patrol`'s loop over the map's spawn points; at a stop she stays only while what's there gives as much EXP a second as going on would, and she shoots and loots on the legs between stops. With the target-first planner (on by default) a stop's fights go one chosen monster at a time and with the whole screen and GAMELAB_LOOT_CHAIN (both on by default) her drops go as a loot chain.
modules.details_md:
Built after the user played 4.5 minutes on Tree Dungeon on 2026-10-24 (484 EXP a minute against the hunt loop's 283 camping one ground): a median 1 s on a platform, a circuit up the tower and back, killing what came into reach on the way.

### What it changes from the hunt loop

- **Where she goes** (`_next_ground`): the next stop by `Patrol.choose` (the loop's next stop worth going to, or a pile of monsters she has seen pulling her off it, or a census trip), after `Patrol.replan` looks for a better loop (`_look_at_round`). Each stop is a `Visit` of the hunt loop to that platform at the stop's x.
- **At a stop** (`_at_ground`, the marginal value theorem: a forager leaves a patch once its rate falls under what the rest of the habitat gives): a monster a star reaches now is shot at once (at her live kill time, 0.085 s a point of EXP, that's 11.8 EXP/s, more than any loop: Tree Dungeon's best is 7.7); otherwise she stays while `_stay_gain` (the held monsters' EXP over their kill time and the walk, less what touches there cost) is at least the bar `max(Plan.rate, the next stop's gain)`. Under it she leaves after `LEAVE_CONFIRM_S` (0.3 s); `STOP_MAX_S` (40 s) is the backstop. No better spot, no lull loot, no rate rule. Held monsters out of reach on another platform: a walk of at most `REACH_STEP` (200) along hers to bring them into reach (rule 'reach').
- **On the legs**: the hunt loop's rule 4 (in passing), 4b (finish) and the sweep's piles on her way. Every `RECHOOSE_S` (1 s) of a trip to a stop, `_interrupt` asks `Patrol.choose` again with that stop as the default; a pile seen elsewhere or "back to the loop" reroutes her.
- **Her drops**: the sweep with only each pile's allowance (`_sweep_terms`: no budget, no lulls; with the planner no MOST_S cap, and the allowance `Targeting.loot_allow`'s); leaving, those on her way to the next stop (`_leave`).
- **What she knows**: every look updates `patrol.Belief` from her memory (`_look`), learns her touches per stop (`_learn_touches`) and prices a bar of HP from her max HP (`_price_hp`, `hunt.bar_exp`).
- **Credit**: each kill is credited to the platform it died on (`credit`), moved when the ledger re-binds a kill (`_book_kills`). The value map (lab/grounds.json) isn't written.

### The target-first planner path

With `behavior.targeting.Targeting` on (`GAMELAB_TARGET`, default on), `_targets` narrows the hunt's targets to the one monster the planner chooses, `_stance` asks the planner's plan, and `_at_ground` becomes `_planned_step`: piles that may go first (`_pile_first`), the plan against the primary, a trip to the place it can be hit from (`_to_place`, objective why "to target"), or `_goes` back to her round when the round clearly beats what the screen has given lately (`GO_GAIN` 1.15). With the whole screen and the loot chain on, `_sweep_act` sends the sweep's next piles as one navigator chain (`_loot_plan`, `behavior.lootchain`), booked by `_chain_over`.

### Records

'grind' telemetry records: `loop` (a new loop taken up), `next` (each stop chosen), `go`, `state` every `STATE_EVERY_S` (60 s), and `end` (stays, pulls, skips, what the belief learned, the census, the loop's promise against what it delivered).

modules.title: The tour (Tour): grounds, the value map, stand-by
modules.tagline: The original sweep of hunting platforms, and the map knowledge the hunt loop builds on.
modules.summary: `Tour` has two jobs. Run by `tour` without `--loop`, it sweeps the map's hunting platforms in a short travel order, shoots each one clear from a safe spot, collects the drops and stands by on a safe platform. And every hunt loop is built over a Tour: it holds the value map (lab/grounds.json), the kinds worth hunting, the safe platforms and the stand-by trip.
modules.details_md:
### Map knowledge (used by Hunt and Grind)

- **Kinds worth hunting** (`worth`): kinds giving at least `WORTH` (0.25) of the map's best EXP a kill; snails (2 against 15) are only shot when in her way.
- **The value map** (`ground_values`): a platform's expected EXP a visit, starting at `SEEN_SHARE` (0.3) of its spawns' EXP and counting as `PRIOR` (2) visits, blended with what real visits gave (`lab/grounds.json`, per map). Only platforms whose spawn kinds her eyes can recognise count.
- **Hunting grounds** (`hunting_grounds`): platforms expected to give at least `MIN_VALUE` (0.15) of the best one's EXP a visit, or, for the hunt loop, its EXP a second (`visit_s`). By EXP a visit, one 351 s visit to the basin once put every other ground under the cut.
- **Safe platforms** (`safe`): `MapModel.safe` and at least `STAND_WIDTH` (120) wide; `stand_by` goes to the nearest one by route time (`nearest_safe`).

### The tour itself (`run`)

1. `sweep` orders the grounds: nearest next by route time with a random +-25%, then 2-opt swaps kept while they save over 0.5 s. A blind random order's median (of 9) is logged for comparison.
2. Each stop (`hunt`, up to `GOES_PER_STOP` 5 goes): go to the spot (stopping on the way where she can stand with a target in reach, `_in_reach`), fight there (`Hunter.clear`, patience 2 s from a spot off the platform, 1 s on it, finishing what's in reach), a whole-screen look for what's left, another spot that reaches it, or onto the platform itself.
3. `collect_loot` goes for remembered drops by route, nearest first: 60 s a trip, none started past `LOOT_SECONDS` (180 s), a guarded pile's guard fought (2 kills, 20 s).
4. The visit is recorded, the rest of the sweep replanned from where she ended up, and finally `stand_by`.

The hunt-modes design kept the old tour "until the loop has passed the game bar in 3 separate sessions".

Note: `Tour.sweep` (the order of grounds) is unrelated to `behavior/sweep.py` (the loot sweep).

modules.title: Patrol: the map's spawn points, stops and loop
modules.tagline: Pure model behind grinding: spawn-point belief, the best loop, and the next stop.
modules.summary: `Patrol` is grinding's knowledge of the map and its choices: every spawn point she hunts, a stop on each platform that reaches some, a `Belief` of how many monsters each point holds now and later, the closed loop of stops that gives the most EXP a minute in the long run, and the choice of the next stop. It is pure: it reads game data, the planner's route times and her memory, and never looks or presses a key.
modules.details_md:
### The map, once

- **Points** (`points_of`): every spawn point of a kind she hunts, with its platform, x, kind and the kind's EXP.
- **Stops** (`stops_of`): on each platform that gets at points, the x (tried every `STAND_STEP`, 20 units) that reaches the most EXP: her own platform's points whole, another's by the share a star reaches (`spots.coverage`), times `1 - STOP_DANGER (2) x danger` there. On Tree Dungeon 31 points and 26 stops.
- **Legs**: route times between stops (`travel`, the planner's `arrive`), cached (`leg`).

### The belief (`Belief`, updated every look)

Each point's monsters (`stock`): those her memory has there; else, for a point seen empty or emptied by her kill, what's back since (`back`: `1 - exp(-rate x dt)`); else, never seen, `Q_UNKNOWN` (0.35). The refill has no memory. The game refills the map to its cap at a pass every `TICK_S` (7.115 s, measured), so the refill rate is her own kills a second over the map's free points (`own / weight`) plus the other players' part (`others`), learned on a grid of rates from points seen free and looked at again within 20 s, weighed by age (180 s), with a gamma prior about `REFILL_RATE` (0.27 a tick). Another player's dot by a point cuts her `share` by `TAKE_WEIGHT x take(kind)`.

**The census** (`_census`, `CENSUS` on): a count by every spawn point, hunted kinds or not, held to the map's cap; kills of hers whose newborn she didn't see are spread over points out of view. **The gate** (`ratio`): when her view's points hold `OCC_MAX` (0.55) or less of the map's average over 60 s, monsters are probably piling elsewhere, and trips open.

### The loop (`best`, `rate`)

A round of 2 to 12 stops, rated in the long run: each point gives its EXP (times her share) times what's back a cycle after she found it free (`caught`); the cycle is travel + 1 s a stop + her shooting (`kill_s` s a point of EXP, learned from her throws); less `hp_price` x the HP touches cost (the danger hook). Grown greedily from the 8 best single stops, adding the stop that raises the rate most at its cheapest place. `replan` takes a new loop only if 15% better, not within 60 s of the last change, unless 3 stops in a row gave nothing.

### The next stop (`choose`)

Along the loop from where she was, the first stop expected to hold `SKIP_FULL` (25%) of its full stock. A stop where she has seen monsters pulls her off the loop when its net EXP pays `PULL_GAIN` (1.25) times what the loop gives over the detour (`pays`). On a pile trip that no longer pays even without the margin: "back to the loop". With the gate open, a census trip (`_trip`): stops off her round believed to hold monsters, taken when their monsters beat 1.25 times her kills a second (over the last 180 s) over the detour.

Before she has seen anything, the module's docstring puts Tree Dungeon's loop at 10, 7 (486 EXP a minute), and `STOP_DANGER`'s comment at 9, 8 (492) since 2026-10-31; the user grinding there made 484.

modules.title: The loot sweep (sweep.plan, Sweeper)
modules.tagline: Which known piles to pick up on her way, and in what order: exact, in seconds.
modules.summary: Pure planner for loot: given pick spots (piles with worth, stand time, landing time, survival, guards and an allowance in seconds) and route times, it returns the itinerary that picks up the most expected mesos within what each pile may add to her way, solved exactly by a dynamic program over subsets. `Sweeper` keeps the itinerary she's on unless another is clearly better.
modules.details_md:
### The problem

An orienteering problem in seconds: choose the set and order of piles that maximises `sum(worth_i x P(still there on arrival))`, subject to:

- each pile alone adds at most its own `allow` to her way (its insertion time, guards' kill times not counted);
- the whole itinerary's `extra` (route through the piles and on to the destination, minus the straight way, minus guards' kills) at most the sum of its piles' allowances, capped at `MOST_S` (6 s; no cap in the hunt loop's lull);
- within `budget` when the hunt loop gives one (a lull's wait, or the way out when leaving).

Of itineraries that pick up as much (to `GAIN_TIE`, 0.1 mesos), the quickest wins.

### The solve (`plan`)

1. Each candidate is checked alone: no route, over its allowance, or expired (survival 0 at its start) is left out with a reason (`Itinerary.out`).
2. The best `MAX_CAND` (8) by worth x survival per second of insertion are kept.
3. A dynamic program over subsets (2^8 masks x 8 last spots) keeps, for each set and last spot, the earliest time she can leave it, the order, and the expected worth (survival taken at each actual arrival).
4. Every (set, last spot) is closed with the leg on to `dest` and checked against the caps; the best key `(round(gain / 0.1), -extra)` wins.

A stop's start is `max(arrival, lands) + guards' kill time`: drops not landed yet are waited for, guards are shot first.

### Keeping an itinerary (`Sweeper.solve`)

Solved again at every look, two piles each worth the other's detour turned her back and forth. So the current itinerary is re-timed (`again`) and kept unless the new one picks up `KEEP_SHARE` (20%) more, as long as it still fits its allowances plus `KEEP_S` (0.5 s).

### What a stand meets (`meets`, `bounce`)

Used by the hunt loop's guards: each monster walks at its velocity, turning back at its platform's walk edges (`bounce`), sampled every `STEP_S` (0.1 s); one with unknown heading may be anywhere it could walk within `UNSURE_S` (1 s). It meets her stand when the gap is under its half width + hers + `CONTACT_MARGIN` (10).

Measured cost (README): 8 candidates a median 2.1 ms (p99 10.5), 6 candidates 0.34 ms; in the simulator's `loop_tree_grind_drops` a solve has a median of 1.5 candidates. The prototype on the live thief run of 2026-10-30 had a median of 3 (8 at most).

modules.title: The loot chain
modules.tagline: Runs through the sweep's next few piles as one navigator chain, pressing pick-up all the way.
modules.summary: The sweep says which piles and in what order; the loot chain says how she goes through them: up to `MOST_PILES` (4) at once, as one key plan of the navigator to each bunch of drops as last seen, pick-up pressed all the way, standing only for the presses a run past wouldn't give. Pure: `Grind` has the looks, the drop store and the navigator; this module is the plan's shape.
modules.details_md:
On when the grind's target-first planner runs with the whole screen and `GAMELAB_LOOT_CHAIN` isn't `'0'` (`on()`; default on).

### Shape

- A `LootChain` holds `Stretch`es in the sweep's order (one per pile), where she goes on to after them (`dest`: her target's place or the next stop), the look it was planned on and the sweep's time estimate.
- A `Stretch` holds a pile's drops as `bunches` (`bunches()`: drops closer than `looting.PILE_GAP`, 15 units, are one bunch, as (middle, count)), the item kinds among them, which bunches she has run over (`ran`), and `again` if she has been through it before.

### The way (`LootChain.way`)

For the navigator's `through`: a list of (platform, x, seconds standing). Each stretch is entered from its end nearer where she comes onto it (`enter`, the planner's `arrive_within`), each bunch a waypoint with `stand_s(n, again)`: `max(0, n - RUN_PRESSES) x 0.12 s` the first time (a run past gives 2 presses for sure at 120 ms a press), `(n + 1) x 0.12 s` if she has been through it and drops still show. `_run_through` merges waypoints she only runs past into the walk that goes on past them.

### Booking (`LootChain.book`)

After the trip, the navigator's record of the stretches she ran over (platform, x from, x to) marks the bunches within `STOOD_ON` (15) of them as done; `Grind._chain_over` turns those into tries and `stood_on`, and what's left is a stop of the next plan.

`END_ROOM` (10) keeps a walk to a drop short of its platform's end; `OFF_END` (60) says a pile no look has seen that far past its platform's end is no pile there (a kill placed wrong); `CHAIN_OFF_S` (0.5 s) sends her the old way (a trip and a stand) after a monster stood in a chain's first walk.

modules.title: Looting (Looter) and what drops are worth
modules.tagline: Picking up after fights, her inventory's tabs, and the price of every drop.
modules.summary: `Looter` is the hunter's looting part: the fights' and the tour's sweeps and mop-ups of drops on her platform, the drops remembered for later, drops she couldn't pick up, and which inventory tabs are full. The module also prices drops in mesos (`Worth`, `PRICES`, `coins_for`, `expected_worth`), which the drop store, the sweep and the valuable-pile rule rank piles by.
modules.details_md:
### Two roles

- **For the tour and fights** (older): `sweep_after` sweeps a fight's kill spots once she has landed; `collect` picks up a remembered spot if it's on her platform and unguarded (no monster within `TOO_CLOSE`), else remembers it in `pending`; `walk_piles` walks from the nearer end of the drops to the far one, `LOOT_REACH` (60) past each end, pressing pick-up and standing on each pile; `mop_up` looks again up to `MOP_UP` (3) times (0.3 s apart) and goes back for what's left; `remember` forgets a spot after two empty looks `EMPTY_LOOKS` (1.5 s) apart, past `SETTLE` (3 s).
- **For the hunt loops**: the drop store (behavior/ledger.py) owns the piles, and the loops clear `pending`. They still rely on the Looter for `can_take`, `wanted`, `cant_pick`, `stood_on`, `on_look`, and the hooks `yield_to` (EXP before loot) and `unseen` (monsters a look missed guard drops). With the loot chain (`store_has_them`), `sweep_after` and `sweep_through` do nothing.

### Inventory tabs (from 2026-10-31)

A drop's tab (`tab_of`) is Use for item ids 2xxxxxx, Etc for 4xxxxxx (mesos none). A tab becomes full (`full`) when drops stay under her after two stands (`cant_pick`) and the pickup log says "You can't get anymore items.", or after `FAILED_PICKS` (3) failures in a row. An "earned. (Tab)" line after the last refusal for a kind that didn't fit says the tab has room. A full tab's items are left, mesos and the other tab still taken; kinds she holds a stack of (`held`) are still taken until one stays under her (`refused`). A full tab is retried after `TAB_RETRY_S` (600 s). A phone push (`push`, control.notify) is sent when a tab fills.

### Worth

Items at the game data's shop price (`PRICES`: e.g. a Slime Bubble 50, a Magic Potion 250, Bronze Ore 20). Mesos by coin: on the first map bronze 15, gold 75; elsewhere `coins_for` averages the amounts the map's monsters drop (Tree Dungeon bronze 33.4, gold 51.5). A drop is valuable at `VALUABLE_COINS` (2) bronze coins. A kill's pile before a look sees it is worth `expected_worth`: 0.64 drops a kill, 57% mesos (live, 2026-10-30).

modules.title: Her stats from perception (HerStats)
modules.tagline: Her max HP, level and DEF read or fitted from perception, never from config.
modules.summary: The "bootstrap" of her stats: her max HP (the HUD's HP number), her level (the HUD's LV. digits, else her EXP number) and her DEF (her stat window's W.DEF, else fitted to her measured touches, else a prior), each with where it came from. The safety stop's HP reserve and the positioning model (attack.danger) are worked out from them; `Hunter` builds one `HerStats` at start and feeds it as perception reads.
modules.details_md:
This is not the hunt's start-up sequence: it's how her character stats get bootstrapped from what perception reads, once the user asked to drop them from config.toml (2026-10-28).

### The three stats

- **Max HP** (`see_max_hp`): the HUD's "HP [cur/max]" number, the moment it reads. Until then a command that hunts waits for it (behavior.safety's `HpNotRead`); the positioning model assumes `PLAN_TOUCHES` (6) of the map's largest touch.
- **Level** (`see_level`): the LV. digits while they read; the EXP number's level once they haven't for `LV_UNREAD_S` (2 s). Until read, `UNREAD_LEVEL` (1), where a touch takes the most.
- **DEF** (`refit`): her stat window's W.DEF (opened and read at a hunt's start by behavior.statcheck), kept in lab/her_stats.json with the level and the perception session it was read in; else `fit_defence` to her last `FIT_N` (40) exact touches; else the prior: `PRIOR_DEF` 0 for the safety stop (the most a touch can take), `PLAN_DEF` (attack.danger's 75) for the positioning model.

### Fitting DEF to touches (`fit_defence`)

For every DEF from 0 to 400 in steps of 0.25, count how many touches some monster of their map could have dealt by the game's formula (`attack.danger.touch_taken` at the touch's level, anywhere in its damage roll). Needs `FIT_MIN` (8) touches and `FIT_AGREE` (80%) agreeing. The `Defence` keeps `low` (the safety stop uses the lowest DEF allowed: the most a touch can take), `high`, and `best` (the prior if inside the range, else the middle). The newest 8 touches are checked separately: if they disagree, gear may have changed, and the lower low is taken or the prior used.

### Doubting a stat-window read (`window_doubt`)

A W.DEF read before this run is doubted if read at another level, in another perception session, or over `SESSION_S` (3 h) before; any read is doubted if her newest touches since don't fit it, or it's above what her touches fit. A W.DEF outside 0-400 is a misread and not taken (an OCR "711" for 111 once put her reserve at 117 HP of 840).

`her()` gives attack.danger the `Her` (HP, level, DEF best) it measures touches against.

modules.title: The movement-only walk
modules.tagline: Random navigator trips over the map, no attack: the live QA walk as one process.
modules.summary: `walk()` sends one monster-avoiding navigator on random trips, one after another, for a number of minutes: `python -m gamelab nav --walk MINUTES`, and the simulator harness's `walk` policy draws the same trips. It tests movement alone, keeping the navigator's tracker, memory and trip state from trip to trip as a hunt would.
modules.details_md:
Each trip goes to a platform drawn at random (`places`): on Tree Dungeon (map 10002073) one of `PLATFORMS` 7-33 (the live QA walk's), elsewhere any platform at least `MIN_WIDTH` (60) wide; an x drawn uniformly `EDGE` (15) in from its ends; `TRIP_S` (40 s) to get there through `nav.go`. Each trip is logged with its result, moves, touches on the way and waits.

`save()` runs every `SAVE_S` (270 s) if given: in the command it asks the rolling recorder (control.rolling) to save its last 300 s as 'qa-walk'. The command (`cmd_nav` -> `_nav_walk` in `gamelab/__main__.py`) runs the walk inside `on_alarm` (the Lie Detector or a stop makes her retreat and ends it), parks her at the end (behavior.retreat.park) and saves once more. With `minutes` None it runs until something stops it, as the harness's horizon does.

It replaced the live QA walk of 2026-10-28 (a script that started `nav` again for each trip), so the navigator's state carries over between trips the way it does in a hunt.

flows.title: One pass of the hunt loop
flows.summary: How a single look turns into a single step, and how a trip hands control back when something new appears.
flows.trigger: Hunt.run's loop (from `tour --loop`), every pass until the minutes run out or a stop.

steps.text: `tour --loop` builds the hunter, a fighting navigator and a Tour, then runs Grind (default) or Hunt (`--camp`) inside on_alarm, and parks at the end.
One report for the hunt; hooks installed on the Looter and Attacks; first ground chosen; then `_pass()` in a loop, standing still on LookLost and running key or stat checks when they're due.

One pass: a look, the bookkeeping, the backstops (the stuck guard, the objective's 60 s clock), then the rules: rule 1 (close quarters) and rule 6a (a valuable pile, only with nothing in reach) first, then `_while_travelling` if an objective is set, else `_at_ground`.
A band look with her platform's drops (the whole screen once a far kill's drops have landed); the 'monsters' record for the mini-map.
New kills from the ledger credited to the visit or 'on the way'; progress clock; fight state reset at a new place or objective.
Potions, and the safety stop when her HP stays low (it raises and ends the hunt).
At the ground: high ground, shoot, better spot, then the rate rule: stay (the sweep's round trip, else wait) or leave (the sweep's piles on the way out, then the next ground).

The step a rule takes first notes it: the rule counted in the report (`rules`, and the seconds until the next note in `rule_s`) and, when the rule changes, the 'hunt' telemetry record sent for the mini-map.
An objective becomes one navigator trip in TRANSIT mode with `until=_interrupt`; `nav.step` until it arrives, stops 'in position', or fails.
Plans and plays chains of moves; before each chain it calls the loop's `_interrupt`.
steps.process: keys go to the elevated key player

steps.text: Whether a rule calls for her now (close quarters, a valuable pile that goes first, a wound to finish, a target she may shoot in passing, a pile the sweep now has): yes stops the trip 'in position' and the next pass decides.

flows.title: Grinding: the loop, the next stop, stay or go
flows.summary: How grinding chooses its round and next stop, and when it leaves a stop.
flows.trigger: The start of the run, then each time she leaves a stop (Grind._next_ground); the stay-or-go check at every pass at a stop.

steps.text: Meanwhile, every look updates Patrol's belief from her memory, learns her touches per stop and prices a bar of HP from her max HP.

At the run's start and whenever she leaves a stop: the round looked at again (`_look_at_round`), then `Patrol.choose` for the next stop; a Visit and a spot objective for it, 'grind' next and 'tour' records.
Learns her kill time from throws and EXP, and asks Patrol.replan on its clock; a new loop is logged and sent as a 'grind' loop record.
Every REPLAN_S (20 s), or at once after 3 stops in a row gave nothing: `Patrol.best`'s round is taken if 15% better than hers and 60 s after the last change.
Grows rounds from the 8 best single stops by cheapest insertion, each rated by Patrol.rate (refill, cycle, HP cost).
The next stop: a census trip in progress, the loop's next stop expected to hold 25% of full, a pull to seen monsters that pays 1.25x the loop over the detour, or a new census trip.
On the leg, every RECHOOSE_S she asks Patrol.choose again; a pull or 'back to the loop' reroutes her at the next pass. Rules 4, 4b and the sweep shoot and loot on the way.
At the stop: shoot what's in reach; otherwise compare `_stay_gain` with max(the loop's rate, the next stop's gain).
Stay while `_stay_gain` is at least max(the loop's rate, the next stop's gain); under it for LEAVE_CONFIRM_S (0.3 s), leave; STOP_MAX_S (40 s) the backstop.
The sweep's piles on her way to the next stop first, then `Patrol.left` (it counts stops that gave nothing) and `_next_ground`.

flows.title: From a kill to its drops picked up
flows.summary: How a kill's pile becomes a stop of the loot sweep, guarded, timed against respawns, and picked up.
flows.trigger: Her EXP number rises and the ledger places the kill: the drop store expects a pile where it died.

steps.text: An expected pile at the kill (drops land about 2 s later), worth its kind's expected drops; looks confirm, update or forget it.

Once a look for each destination: pick spots from the store's candidates (`_spots`), the terms (`_sweep_terms`: a lull's wait as the budget, or what's left of her way out's), then the sweeper's solve; a 'sweep' record when the itinerary changes.
Each candidate pile becomes a sweep.Spot: worth she can take, stand time, landing, survival, guards (`_guards`) and allowance (`_allow`).
The exact best itinerary on her way (or a round trip, or her way out), kept unless another is 20% better.
Guards shot first; by the pile, wait for the landing or stand; else a trip there.
The spawn guard may hold a short trip for the respawn pass; else a pile objective is pushed and travelled to.
On arrival: each bunch walked to and pressed (a press per drop plus one), a try counted, a 'pick' event.
Drops still under her after two stands are left 90 s; the pickup log tells whether a tab is full.
In grinding with the planner and loot chain on, the itinerary's next 4 piles go as one navigator chain (LootChain.way), booked by Grind._chain_over.

steps.text: Hunting grounds by the value map, ordered by Tour.sweep; the blind random order's travel logged for comparison.
Nearest next by route time with a random +-25%, then 2-opt on real route times.
Up to 5 goes: to the spot (stopping where a target is in reach and she can stand), a fight, a whole-screen look for what's left, another spot or onto the platform.
The fight at the spot (behavior.fight): kills in reach, finishes far ones, with the stop's patience.
Trips to remembered drops, nearest first, 60 s each, none after 180 s; Looter.collect picks up or fights the guard.
`Tour.hunt` ends by recording the visit (visits and EXP) in lab/grounds.json; back in `Tour.run`, the rest of the sweep is replanned from where she ended up.
To the nearest safe platform at least 120 wide, to stand by.

not_done: gamelab/docs/hunt-modes.md's status line still lists step 6, the game trials against the bar, as to do; the old tour was to stay until the loop passed it in 3 sessions.
RESPAWN (8 s, the simulator's) isn't settled by live telemetry: the game may not refill a platform she empties that way; it stays until the in-game check.
Not built (hunt-modes.md): the whole-screen loot look about 3 s after each kill, and "the same objective dropped 3 times" in the stuck guard.
Most thresholds are marked "guess" (PULL_GAIN, LOOP_GAIN, STOP_MAX_S, REACH_STEP, RECHOOSE_S, TRIP_AHEAD_S, CHAIN_OFF_S and more): tuned in the simulator harness, not measured in game.
Drop ownership (15 s, ledger.OWN_S) and how often other players take the piles she leaves aren't measured.
The loot chain's RUN_PRESSES (2) is read from the simulator's reach and her speed, not tried live.
Whether her pet picks up what she walks past is only estimated from recordings; PET_LOOT stays off.
The target-first planner is on by default though its second gate wasn't passed (behavior/targeting.py).
Drops lying at a stop aren't counted in the next stop's choice (DROPS_IN_CHOICE was tried and left off).
BACK (going back to the stop when a knock leaves her somewhere more dangerous) is built but off by the user's choice of more EXP and loot.
A sweep guard is shot only from where she is now, not from a place along her way; one she can't shoot from there leaves the pile out for that look.
One map at a time: portals and other maps are out of scope (hunt-modes.md open questions).
